title.why: Which value the stored text supports: the first extraction's. Page 5 of the bill is headed 'BAZI KANUNLARDA DEGiSIKLIK YAPILMASINA ÏLÏSKÏN KANUN TEKLiFi' (OCR of 'Bazı Kanunlarda Değişiklik Yapılmasına İlişkin Kanun Teklifi'), which is 'Bill on Amendments to Certain Laws'. The old title (and the blind extraction, which kept it) followed the cover letter's running sentence '5237 sayılı ve 26/9/2004 tarihli Türk Ceza Kanunu ve Bazı Kanunlarda değişiklik yapılmasına dair kanun teklifini gerekçesi ile birlikte ekte sunulmuştur', which is also real text but a sentence fragment with the date clause, not the bill's own heading. The Turkish press and Hukuki Haber use the cover-letter wording, so a reader may know the bill by it; the descriptive parenthetical in the record's English title (Penal Code, AI provisions, 2/3358) keeps it findable. Defensible either way; the first extraction's is the more literal.

original_title.why: Page 5 heading, read through OCR: 'BAZI KANUNLARDA DEGiSIKLIK YAPILMASINA ÏLÏSKÏN KANUN TEKLiFi'. The record's 'Bazı Kanunlarda Değişiklik Yapılmasına İlişkin Kanun Teklifi' restores Turkish letters; I read 'ÏLÏSKÏN' as 'İLİŞKİN' (the OCR dropped the cedilla on S), and the same heading wording appears in Turkish bills generally. Only the diacritics are inferred; the letters match. Word for word, 'İlişkin' ('relating to') and the cover letter's 'dair' ('concerning') are alternatives; the heading uses 'İlişkin'.

issuing_body.why: Cover letter signed 'Av. Halil ÖZTÜRK Kırıkkale Milletvekili' on MHP group letterhead, addressed to the TBMM Speaker.

official_identifier.why: Stamp 'Tarih: 10-11-2025 |Esas No:2/3358'. '28th term, 4th legislative year' is not in the text; it comes from the official_url path (D28/Y4); acceptable.

date_published.why: TBMM receipt stamp '07 Kasim 2025' on page 2. The signature date is 23/7/2025 (cover letter) and registration 10-11-2025; the record uses receipt by the Assembly, which the notes explain.

status.why: Draft / proposed. The bill is registered with committee referrals; nothing stored shows a committee report or vote. One web search (Turkish press, Hukuki Haber, Haber7) found no newer stage; the press still describes it as submitted in September 2025.

summary.why: Each claim found in the Turkish text; see summary_claims. The summary names 'transparency and auditability of training data, content verification, hallucination controls and human-approved oversight' (Art. 6 a to d) and leaves out e (regular cybersecurity vulnerability tests); acceptable.

notes.why: Signature 23/7/2025, receipt 7 Nov 2025, registration 10 Nov 2025, Esas No. 2/3358 and the lead (Sanayi, Ticaret, Enerji, Tabii Kaynaklar, Bilgi ve Teknoloji) and secondary committees (Adalet; Dijital Mecralar) are in the page 1 stamp. 11 articles and entry into force on publication: Art. 10 'Bu Kanun yayımı tarihinde yürürlüğe girer'. Art. 1 definition of AI system in Law 5651 Art. 2; Art. 4 datasets: 'anonimlik, ayrımcılık yasağı ve meşruiyet ilkelerine uygun olmak zorundadır. Ayrımcı veri setlerinin kullanılması veri güvenliğinin ihlali sayılır'; Art. 2 penalty for the developer 'yarı oranında artırılır' (increased by half); Art. 8 adds insult, threat and crimes against humanity (items 8 to 10) to the Law 5651 Art. 8 list.

summary_claims.claim: A user who directs an AI system to a criminal act is its perpetrator
summary_claims.locator: page 5, Art. 2: '(6) Yapay zekâ sistemlerini bu kanun uyarınca suç sayılan bir fiile yönlendiren kullanıcı, bu suçun faili sayılır ve buna göre cezalandırılır.' = 'A user who directs AI systems to an act that is a crime under this law is regarded as the perpetrator of that crime and punished accordingly.'

summary_claims.claim: Removal or blocking within six hours of AI content that violates personality rights, threatens public security or is a deepfake
summary_claims.locator: page 5, Art. 3: '...kişilik haklarına aykırı, kamu güvenliğini tehdit eden veya deepfake teknolojisi kullanılarak gerçek dışı şekilde düzenlenen içerikler hakkında erişim engelleme ve içerik kaldırma işlemleri 6 saat içinde yerine getirilir.' = 'access blocking and content removal for content produced by AI systems that violates personality rights, threatens public security, or is made untrue using deepfake technology is carried out within 6 hours.'

summary_claims.claim: Non-removable 'Produced by Artificial Intelligence' label on deepfakes; fines TRY 500,000 to 5 million
summary_claims.locator: page 6, Art. 7 (Ek madde 5): 'açık, anlaşılır ve silinemez bir ibare ... “Yapay Zekâ Tarafından Üretilmiştir”' and 'BTK tarafından ... 500.000 TL ile 5.000.000 TL arasında idari para cezası'. = 'a clear, understandable and non-erasable statement ... "Produced by Artificial Intelligence"'; 'an administrative fine between TL 500,000 and TL 5,000,000 by BTK'.

page 5, Art. 5: 'BTK, kamu düzenini veya seçim güvenliğini tehdit eden yapay zeka içerikleri hakkında acil erişim engelleme kararı verebilir' = 'BTK may issue an urgent access-blocking decision on AI content threatening public order or election security'.

scope.note: Pending bill with AI-specific provisions (deepfake labelling, provider duties); in scope, with Legal force Proposed. Private member's bill with uncertain prospects; the instrument is AI-specific so no scope_note is needed, though the human may add one for 'little chance of passing' if the register wants it.

note: The updated title, original_title, summary and notes match the stored scan of the bill (OCR layer, Turkish letters restored by the extractor), and the evidence script found no errors (level A on the official PDF). I translated the Art. 2, 3, 5 and 7 passages and they match the summary, including the must/may and the penalties. Blind-sample difference on title and original_title: the blind extraction left the old cover-letter wording; the text supports the first extraction's heading-based values and also the old wording, so either passes; I prefer the first. The Turkish diacritics in original_title are inferred from OCR, a small caveat. No newer stage found in one web search.
